output.best_reason: Version C builds the most tension by withholding. Rosa's refusal to say whether she saw Madame go up the stairs, her "I did not hear her cry," and her fixation on the glasses left on the tray all carry suspicion without stating it. Its facts come out in answer to Matthey's questions, so they feel like testimony rather than a list. Its closing line about the clock is a strong character note. Its flaw is that Matthey calls the maid "Fräulein Ruedi" while Rosa and the rest of the text say "Fräulein Lina," which is a continuity slip to fix. Version A is the warmest and has a vivid, consistent voice, with the Emmental detail and the kitchen rhythm, but it is more cosy than tense. Version B has a good voice and a sharp "you are frightened of me, I think" beat, but it front-loads exposition about the master, inventories the crime scene (blood, mallet, regulator, watch) in one speech, and inconsistently addresses Rosa as "Madame Häfeli" and then "Rosa."
